findings.title: Section 7(a): parties swapped, so the protection against unagreed additional terms now runs to You instead of the Licensor
findings.description: In A, Section 7(a) says the Licensor is not bound by additional or different terms that You communicate unless it expressly agrees. In B the roles are reversed: You are not bound by additional or different terms that the Licensor communicates. The protection the clause gives the Licensor is gone, and B gives a new protection to the licensee. This changes who is bound by what between the parties, and a reader would act on it.

evidence.quote: The Licensor shall not be bound by any additional or different terms or conditions communicated by You unless expressly agreed.
You shall not be bound by any additional or different terms or conditions communicated by the Licensor unless expressly agreed.

findings.title: Privileges-and-immunities clause moved from Section 8(d) (Interpretation) to Section 7(c) (Other Terms and Conditions)
findings.description: In A, the clause saying nothing in the license limits or waives the privileges and immunities of the Licensor or You is item d of Section 8 -- Interpretation. In B the same wording is item c of Section 7 -- Other Terms and Conditions. The wording is unchanged and the clause still applies to the whole license, so the practical effect is small. However, it now sits under a different heading and has a new letter, so any outside citation to 'Section 8(d)' no longer points to it. In B, Section 8 now ends at c with no gap in the lettering.

evidence.quote: d. Nothing in this Public License constitutes or may be interpreted as a limitation upon, or waiver of, any privileges and immunities
c. Nothing in this Public License constitutes or may be interpreted as a limitation upon, or waiver of, any privileges and immunities

coverage_note: Chunk c02 has ops 71-74, all of them in Section 7. Op 71 (EQUAL: Section 7 heading) and op 73 (EQUAL: 7(b) on separate arrangements) were context only and were not judged as changes. Op 72 (MODIFIED) is reported as a critical 'changed' finding because the parties in 7(a) are swapped. Op 74 (MOVED) is reported as a minor 'moved' finding: the clause went from 8(d) to 7(c) and its wording is unchanged. To check op 74, I also read the source files and confirmed that in B, Section 8 is lettered a-c with no gap, so the move leaves no broken lettering. No op in this chunk was dismissed as editorial, and nothing was left unjudged.
